lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet can be revealing in Toronto. Sergei Bobrovsky's arrival has already changed the temperature at camp - not with noise, but with authority, the kind of veteran calm that settles a room and sharpens a crease. That matters for a club that finished 48-28-6 and now has to turn the page without the luxury of illusion. Bobrovsky says the job is simple: stop pucks, give the team a chance, and let the rest sort itself out. Around him, the real camp question is whether rookie Gavin McKenna earns a bigger power-play bite or is eased in behind the veterans. Auston Matthews remains the standard, but leadership in this market is always judged by posture as much as production. Next comes the final cut-down pressure and a long look at how this roster fits before opening night.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season's wreckage has already been swept into the corner, and now the Blue Jays are left with the hard, unfashionable work of sorting through what survives. Housekeeping looms after a season of roster churn - and that is no metaphor, with the 40-man roster crowded at 39, eight free agents pending, and seven players on the 60-day IL waiting to be restored. Toronto's final record is buried in the rearview; what matters now is how aggressively it trims, protects, and retools before winter bites. Max Scherzer and Chris Bassitt headline the sort of name game that still gives this club some heft, while rookies and depth arms like Trey Yesavage and Tom Cellucci have forced their way into the conversation. Watch the roster moves next, because the Blue Jays' offseason begins with subtraction before any hope of addition.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The quiet of September has been broken by a loud, expensive decision - and it tells you everything about Toronto's intentions. Kawhi Leonard agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors, a deal that says the franchise is done flirting with half-measures and ready to build around a star again. The club finished 2025-26 at 48-34, a respectable mark that still left room for a bigger swing, and this is it. Leonard is the hinge now - the health gamble, the ceiling raiser, the name that changes the room. Allen Graves offers draft intrigue, Bobby Webster has more cap-room sleight of hand to consider, and the roster is still taking shape. What matters next is camp, and whether Toronto can turn this headline into a functioning team before the real work begins.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders' offseason has turned into a quarterback triage unit - again. Jayden Daniels' elbow and the surgery call hanging over it are the story now, because everything else flows from that one decision. Marcus Mariota is the bridge, and the bridge better hold: Washington went 2-6 with him starting in 2025, and that history explains why this feels less like a detour than a warning light. The good news, if there is any, is that the offense has a cleaner identity with Rachaad White's receiving skill giving Mariota a reliable outlet. Washington finished 2025 at 10-7, but that record only sharpens the pressure on what comes next. Watch the medical ruling on Daniels, then the ripple effect on the depth chart, because the entire autumn plan depends on it.

article.title: Wednesday's Skate
paragraphs: Bobrovsky is already leaving a mark at Leafs camp, with coverage out of Toronto framing him as a steady, veteran presence in the room. That sort of tone matters in September, when the work is less about box scores and more about building habits.

The Blue Jays head to Game 1 of the doubleheader with Max Scherzer lined up against Chris Bassitt at Camden Yards. The Raptors are still in offseason mode, but talk around the club continues to circle Bobby Webster and the possibility of another move, while the Commanders are facing a tougher morning after Jayden Daniels' elbow injury pushed Marcus Mariota into the spotlight.
